title: The Desert That Feeds a Jungle

script.text: The Amazon rainforest is fertilized by the Sahara Desert.

script: Some of it starts here: the [Bodélé|Bo-deh-lay] Depression in Chad, the dustiest place on Earth.
Around [7,000|seven thousand] years ago, this was a lake bigger than Germany.

script.text: When it dried, it left a floor of fossil algae, rich in phosphorus.

script: Winds lift it into the sky, and carry it west across the Atlantic.
On average, [182|one hundred and eighty-two] million tons of dust leave the Sahara every year.
[132|One hundred and thirty-two] million are still in the air off South America.

script.text: And [27.7|twenty-seven point seven] million tons fall on the Amazon.

script: Hidden inside: about [22,000|twenty-two thousand] tons of phosphorus.

script.text: Roughly what the rainforest loses every year, washed away by rain and floods.

script: The jungle's soil is poor. The desert tops it up.
The largest hot desert on Earth, feeding the largest rainforest.
